title: The investment profession: ethics, compliance, performance standards and careers
audience: a finance graduate or career changer preparing for the CFA Program exams and a career in investment analysis
purpose: Practice the professional side of investing: apply the CFA Institute Code and Standards to workplace dilemmas, follow compliance and conflict-of-interest rules, present performance under the GIPS standards, understand licensing such as the SIE and Series 7, serve clients as a fiduciary, and plan a career with networking, interviews and continuing education.
primary_reading: CFA Institute: Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct

weeks.1: Professionalism and the Code and Standards
weeks.3: Conflicts of interest and personal trading
weeks.9: Careers: roles in investment management, research and banking
weeks.12: Technology, AI and the future of the profession

blocks.deliverable: Resolve five workplace dilemmas with the Standards.
Write a personal-trading policy for a small firm.
Map which license each role needs.
Week 7 midterm; review a performance presentation for errors.
Draft a resume and three interview stories.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Professional portfolio: a written ethics case analysis with your resolution, a compliance checklist for a new advisory firm, a review of a sample GIPS presentation, and a career plan with a targeted resume and interview stories.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
